name: Gongura Mamsam
subtitle: mutton braised with sour sorrel leaves, the dish Andhra is judged by

ingredients.note: bone matters here, the gravy is thin without it
standing in for gongura (sorrel); if you find gongura use it and cut the tamarind by half
only to make up the sourness the substitute lacks
Guntur if you can get them

prepNotes: The greens go in twice. Half early, to melt into the gravy, half at the end so something still tastes green.
Gongura is aggressively sour. If you are using amaranth, the tamarind is doing the work the leaf would.

steps.text: Wilt the greens in a dry pan until they collapse and give up their water, about 5 minutes. Set aside.
steps.tip: No oil. You want them dry, not fried.

steps.text: Brown the onion in the oil until properly dark. Add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook out the raw smell.
Add the mutton, turmeric, coriander powder and chillies. Fry on high until the meat is sealed and colouring.
steps.tip: Do not add salt yet, it draws water and stews the meat.

steps.text: Add 250ml water and the tamarind, cover and cook 50 minutes until the mutton yields, or 5 whistles in a pressure cooker.
Stir in half the wilted greens and simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the gravy tightens around the meat.
Fold in the rest of the greens, salt to taste, and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves overnight as the sourness settles into the meat. Reheat gently with a splash of water. Freezes well for a month.
